reason: S1 adds the experimental entry point meshopt_optimizeMeshletLevel and a new level parameter whose values 1 through 9 select newly introduced valence- and cache-distance-based behavior. H0 never calls this entry point and cannot control level; the existing meshopt_optimizeMeshlet wrapper always supplies 0. This commit therefore creates a material, commit-induced coverage gap for the new API and its nonzero-level behavior.
evidence: src/meshoptimizer.h newly declares meshopt_optimizeMeshletLevel(..., int level) and documents level in [0, 9].
meshopt_optimizeMeshletLevel asserts level >= 0 && level <= 9 and enters a distinct `if (level)` scoring path using `valence`, cache distances, and an `edges >= level` stopping condition.
meshopt_optimizeMeshlet delegates to meshopt_optimizeMeshletLevel(..., 0), so exercising the legacy entry point cannot reach the level>0 branch.

H0 calls meshopt_buildMeshlets, meshopt_buildMeshletsScan, meshopt_buildMeshletsFlex, meshopt_buildMeshletsSpatial, meshopt_partitionClusters, codec functions, and simplification functions, but never meshopt_optimizeMeshletLevel or meshopt_optimizeMeshlet.
recommended_action: Extend a meshlet fuzz harness to construct valid meshlet vertex and triangle arrays, call meshopt_optimizeMeshletLevel, and derive level across the documented 0–9 range from fuzz input, with particular coverage of levels 1–9.
